acceptedFindings.title: P-values reported as 0.0000 violate ASA guidelines and are misleading
evidenceRefs: stats-run.json estimates: extremely small actual p-values (e.g., 1.97e-30)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Reporting p-values as 0.0000 gives a false impression of zero probability, overstates precision, and deviates from standard scientific reporting. ASA guidelines recommend reporting exact p-values or a threshold (e.g., <0.001).
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Replace all 'p=0.0000' with the exact p-values (e.g., <0.001 or scientific notation) and add a note about p-value interpretation.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that no p-value is literally displayed as 0.0000 in the manuscript or tables.

acceptedFindings.title: Outcome, exposure, and covariate variables are not defined
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md Methods/Variables: 'Outcome: outcome_cont. Exposure or predictor: severity. Covariates: age, treatment.'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without operational definitions, measurement scales, or coding, the results cannot be interpreted, replicated, or compared to other studies. Readers do not know what a 1-unit change in severity or outcome_cont represents.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a Variables section defining each variable: its role, measurement units, continuous/categorical nature, and any transformation. Describe 'treatment' coding (e.g., 0/1).

acceptedFindings.title: No confounding adjustment plan or rationale for covariates
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md Methods/Covariates: only age and treatment
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Observational studies with arbitrary covariate selection produce biased adjusted estimates. Without a directed acyclic graph (DAG) or subject-matter justification, the adjusted coefficient for severity may be confounded, and the claim of 'association after adjustment' is potentially misleading.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a minimally sufficient adjustment set based on domain knowledge or a DAG, or explicitly state that the model is purely descriptive with no causal interpretation and discuss likely residual confounding.

acceptedFindings.title: Key regression assumptions (linearity, homoscedasticity) not checked
evidenceRefs: diagnostics.json includes Shapiro-Wilk, VIF, Cook's D, but no Breusch-Pagan test or residual-vs-fitted plot inspection
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The linear regression model assumes linear relationships and constant error variance. Violations can invalidate standard errors, confidence intervals, and p-values. The reported diagnostics are insufficient to confirm model appropriateness.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report tests for heteroscedasticity (e.g., Breusch-Pagan) and linearity checks (e.g., partial residual plots). If violations exist, consider robust standard errors, transformations, or non-linear terms.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that diagnostics include at least one formal test for homoscedasticity and a comment on linearity for continuous predictors.

acceptedFindings.title: Complete-case analysis without missing data investigation
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md Limitations: 'missingness may affect the result'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: If missingness is non-ignorable or related to exposure/outcome, complete-case estimates can be biased. No report of missing proportions, patterns, or sensitivity analysis is provided.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Describe the amount and pattern of missing data for all variables. Perform sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation as a supplementary analysis) or justify why complete cases are defensible.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Require a missingness table or figure in supplementary material.

acceptedFindings.title: Artifact count mismatch and lack of analysis code or data
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The discrepancy undermines the claimed reproducibility. Essential elements (analysis code, raw data) are not included in the artifacts, so independent verification is impossible.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Reconcile the artifact inventory; include all relevant scripts, data dictionaries, and a README. Ensure the artifact count matches the actual files.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Count files in the run directory and verify they match the reported number.

acceptedFindings.title: Model fit (R-squared) not reported
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md Results only shows coefficient estimates
diagnostics.json includes AIC/BIC but no R-squared
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without an overall measure of explained variance, the practical significance of the model is unclear. R-squared helps assess whether the model captures meaningful signal in the outcome.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report R-squared (or adjusted R-squared) and comment on its magnitude relative to typical benchmarks in the domain.

acceptedFindings.title: Incorrect statement about influence diagnostics
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md Limitations: 'No explicit influence diagnostic evidence was found.'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript falsely claims no influence diagnostics exist, but Cook's distance values are present. This erodes trust in the carefulness of the reporting.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Correct the statement to reflect that influence diagnostics were examined (max Cook's D = 0.078) and no influential observations were identified.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the limitation text acknowledges the available Cook's distance.
